slides.title: TacPrint: A Wearable Fingertip Tactile Sensor for Human-to-Robot Contact Reproduction
slides.tldr: WEARABLE FINGERTIP TACTILE SENSOR FOR CONTACT REPRODUCTION
slides.highlight: TacPrint enables fine-grained tactile data collection for human-to-robot skill transfer, supporting the MOSAIC goal of estimating procedural and tacit skills through physics-based sensing.

card.one_liner: TacPrint is a low-cost wearable fingertip sensor that recovers dense contact-depth maps from sparse capacitive signals.
card.key_idea: A wearable sensor with 24 taxel-aligned silicone protrusions uses a real-to-sim-to-real LSTM-based pipeline to estimate 35×26 contact-depth maps from sparse capacitive measurements.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via controlled indentations, human-to-robot replay (grasping/wiping), and closed-loop grasping. Results show high success rates (up to 91.67%) and low depth error (0.085mm).
card.limitation: Sparse 24-channel input limits detailed shape reconstruction, and predictions may retain characteristics of the training indenters.

slides.title: FasTac: A Curved Multispectral Vision-Based Tactile Sensor for High-Speed High-Precision 3D Shape and Force Perception
slides.highlight: FasTac enables high-precision 3D shape and three-axis force perception, supporting the physics- and force-based human proficiency estimation required for MOSAIC.

card.one_liner: FasTac is a curved vision-based tactile sensor for high-speed 3D shape and three-axis force perception.
card.key_idea: Integrates RGB-NIR multispectral imaging for 3D reconstruction, a position-aware dynamic-convolution network (HyperForce) for force estimation, and FPGA hardware acceleration.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via 3D reconstruction and force tasks; achieved depth MAE of 0.0415mm, force NMAE < 2.74%, and 1.09ms FPGA latency.
card.limitation: The FPGA deployment is limited to the normal-force branch (Fz) due to buffering and computation resource constraints.

slides.title: τ: Learning Touch-Augmented Vision-Language-Action Models from Future Visual Supervision
slides.tldr: TOUCH-AUGMENTED VLA FRAMEWORK FOR CONTACT-RICH MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This framework integrates spatiotemporal tactile representations into VLA models using future visual supervision to improve robustness in contact-rich tasks.

card.one_liner: τ is a touch-augmented VLA framework that improves contact-rich manipulation using future visual supervision.
card.key_idea: Integrates a tactile encoder and adapter into a pretrained VLA, using a JEPA-style auxiliary branch to predict future visual feature changes from action-conditioned tactile representations during training.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the new TacAura dataset across four contact-rich tasks; outperformed VLA and VTLA baselines in success rates and zero-shot generalization.
card.limitation: Computational constraints prevented comparison with tactile-aware world models; cross-task, cross-embodiment, and cross-sensor transferability remain unexplored.

slides.title: MDIR: A Task-Manifold Impedance Retargeting Method for Contact-Rich Teleoperation
slides.highlight: MDIR reduces force variability and impact in contact-rich tasks by reparameterizing fixed Cartesian impedance into task-channel variable-impedance commands. This is relevant to MOSAIC's focus on physics and force-based skill acquisition and human-AI intent alignment.

card.one_liner: MDIR retargets fixed-impedance teleoperation demonstrations into variable-impedance controllers to reduce interaction aggressiveness while preserving task success.
card.key_idea: It decomposes demonstrations into work, exertion, and support channels using a control-chain metric, then optimizes parameters to minimize force peaks and power under response-preserving constraints.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a Franka Panda across wiping, pick-and-place, and pushing tasks; MDIR passed all 15 closed-loop executions and reduced four aggressiveness metrics.
card.limitation: MPO may increase pose deviation by exploiting geometric slack in non-critical directions to achieve gentler interaction.

slides.title: FA-RDP: A Frequency-Adaptive Reactive Diffusion Policy for Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.tldr: FREQUENCY-ADAPTIVE DIFFUSION POLICY FOR CONTACT-RICH TASKS
slides.highlight: FA-RDP addresses the tradeoff between action multimodality and reactivity in contact-rich manipulation by dynamically switching between low-frequency multi-step sampling and high-frequency one-step sampling.

card.one_liner: FA-RDP adapts inference frequency to balance pre-contact multimodality and post-contact reactivity in manipulation.
card.key_idea: A shared visual-force Transformer uses a learned multimodality indicator to switch between multi-step low-frequency sampling and one-step high-frequency sampling via Manifold Consistency Distillation.
card.evaluation: Tested on three real-world contact-rich tasks; achieved 81.7% average success rate, outperforming baselines like ImplicitRDP and RDP.
card.limitation: Requires a three-stage training procedure and is currently limited to single-task policies using only visual-force inputs.

slides.title: TacWAM: Anchor-Guided World Action Model with Mechanics-Aware Tactile Prediction
slides.tldr: TACTILE-AWARE WORLD ACTION MODEL FOR CONTACT-RICH MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: TacWAM introduces a mechanics-aware world action model that uses tactile futures to supervise action learning, improving success rates in contact-rich manipulation tasks.

card.one_liner: TacWAM improves contact-rich manipulation by using future tactile predictions as training supervision for action generation.
card.key_idea: A tri-modal WAM using a Spatially Aligned Fusion encoder for mechanics-aware tactile representations and Anchor-Guided Attention to isolate future targets from action tokens.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on four real-world tasks (e.g., fragile grasping, wiping); achieved 75.0% average success rate, beating the strongest baseline by 37.5 percentage points.

slides.title: TRACT: Temporally Routed Action Chunks with Chronological Phase Authority for Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.tldr: ROUTED ACTION CHUNKING FOR CONTACT-RICH MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: TRACT addresses temporal mismatches in action chunking for contact-rich tasks, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on procedural skill acquisition and human-AI intent alignment.

card.one_liner: TRACT improves contact-rich manipulation by decoupling current phase authority from future action chunk routing.
card.key_idea: It uses a chronological phase manager for present state and a monotone cumulative boundary distribution to route future queries between current and successor phases.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a real-robot planar-wiping task (10 trials/variant); full TRACT achieved 10/10 success and 99% wipe completion versus 3/10 for flat conditioning.
card.limitation: Limited to one fixed-scene task and assumes at most one phase transition per generated action horizon.

slides.title: ACE-Data-0: Human-Centric Ambient Capture as Embodied Data Engine
slides.tldr: MULTISENSORY EMBODIED DATA ENGINE FOR HUMAN-CENTRIC CAPTURE
slides.highlight: The Ambient Capture Engine (ACE) provides a unified multisensory stream of human demonstrations across household activities, supporting the development of embodied social robots and AI-mediated interaction for RwB.

card.one_liner: ACE-Data-0 is a large-scale, multi-modal dataset of human-object interactions in realistic home environments.
card.key_idea: The Ambient Capture Engine (ACE) uses table-scale and room-scale configurations to synchronize egocentric/exocentric video, motion capture, 6-DoF object trajectories, audio, and tactile signals.
card.evaluation: Evaluated 30+ SOTA methods via a hierarchical benchmark (signals, components, interactions); results showed significant gaps under occlusion and long horizons.
